rule.question: Which registrant did this counterparty name refer to, when SEC's list of current filers does not contain it?
rule.the_search_only_generates_candidates: EDGAR's company search is an undocumented prefix match; it returned different results for 'Marconi' and 'Marconi Communications', and its multi-hit XML carries ARRAY(0x...) where the company name should be. Nothing is accepted on its say-so.
rule.acceptance_is_the_lineage_test: A candidate CIK is accepted only if peer_lineage.assess returns CONTINUOUS against that registrant's own submissions record: filing on the disclosure date, under a matching name. Two accepted registrants is AMBIGUOUS and resolves to nothing.
rule.no_form_type_filter: type=10-K silently excludes foreign private issuers, who file 20-F. Filtering would make 'no such registrant' indistinguishable from 'files a different form'.
rule.a_resolved_registrant_may_not_trade: Identifying the registrant and finding it has no current ticker is a RESULT, not a failure: it converts an inference about the method into a documented fact about a named company, which is what a survivorship statement needs.
rule.curates_nothing: No edge is written and no candidate is promoted. The display gate is untouched.

what_this_is: Which registrant each of 6 extracted competitor/supplier counterparty names (from the input above) referred to, and whether that registrant still trades.
what_this_is_not: Curation. No edge is written to any linkage map, no peer universe is derived here. peer_selection.py's evaluate_peer() is the next, separate step, and needs point-in-time market cap (shares_outstanding.py + point_in_time_market_cap.py) for whatever resolves here first.
unanswered_is_not_a_negative: A name whose search failed is UNANSWERED, not evidence the company doesn't exist -- an endpoint outage deciding a result is the failure this project refuses everywhere else.
